issues.description: Silent semantic change: coerceNumber maps null/undefined to 0 instead of propagating NaN as the old toNumber did.
issues.detail: The original panLinear/zoomLinear passed toNumber as the lift, so non-numeric domain entries propagated as null/NaN downstream. The new coerceNumber substitutes 0, silently distorting the domain instead of failing loudly. This is a real behavior change buried in a 'just added types' PR. Either preserve NaN propagation or document the new contract in the commit message.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] via Math.sign before the isNonEmpty guard inside pan/zoom fires.
issues.detail: Math.sign(domain[0]) executes at the public entry point before delegating to pan/zoom, so an empty domain yields Math.sign(undefined)=NaN before the error is thrown. The precondition is asserted in the wrong place. Hoist the non-empty check to each public entry, or assert it before computing sign.

issues.description: Domain parameter typed as number[] when NonEmptyArray<number> is what the API actually requires.
issues.detail: Public signatures advertise number[] but the body refines via isNonEmpty. Pushing NonEmptyArray<number> to the boundary would make the contract checkable by callers at compile time and reduce the runtime guard to a backstop. Half-typed is worse than fully typed; the type system already supports the stronger precondition.

issues.description: Empty-domain throw is only tested for panLinear/zoomLinear; the other six entry points are unproven.
issues.detail: panLog, panPow, panSymlog, zoomLog, zoomPow, zoomSymlog share the same empty-domain precondition but no test exercises them. Given the Log/Pow ordering issue above, this is exactly the testing-shows-presence trap. A table-driven test over all eight entry points would prove the contract cheaply.

issues.description: Local identity reintroduces a utility that already exists in accessors.js.
issues.detail: The original file imported identity from ./accessors.js; the new file inlines a typed identity and adds a typed coerceNumber wrapper. Functionally equivalent, but it duplicates a shared utility and diverges from codebase voice. Fix the type of the shared identity/toNumber once and keep one definition.

issues.description: peek overload pair is more machinery than the data shape needs.
issues.detail: Two overloads plus an implementation signature for a one-line array[length-1]. If callers used NonEmptyArray at the boundary, peek would not need an overload at all. The non-empty overload also relies on a type-level promise the implementation does not formally discharge under noUncheckedIndexedAccess.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the refactor is a mostly faithful TypeScript port with one substantive semantic regression: coerceNumber silently maps null to 0 where the original toNumber propagated null/NaN, a behavior change hidden inside a 'just types' PR. The empty-domain guard is also misplaced for Log/Pow variants, which read domain[0] before the isNonEmpty check fires, and only Linear is tested. Structurally, the public Domain type should be NonEmptyArray<number> at the boundary so the runtime guard becomes a backstop rather than the sole line of defense. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — fix the coercion semantics (or own it in the commit), broaden empty-domain tests, and tighten the Domain input type.
